To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the anti-tumour activity of cSAL is enhanced by the replacement of aspartic acid and glutamic acid residues with asparagine, glutamine, and arginine, with the replacement of D2 and E88 with arginine being the most effective.
the anti-tumour effect of the bullfrog sialyl binding lectin (SBL) is enhanced by the introduction of a positive charge into its molecule.

the replacement of the aspartic/glutamic acid residue of bullfrog sialoglycoprotein binding lectin with arginine and glutamine/asparagine increases the anti-tumor and internalization efficiency of the lectin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of charge of cSBN on its anti-tumor activity in murine leukemia cells.
the relationship between the structure and anti-tumor effect of the sialic acid-binding lectin, cSBL.

the relationship between the charge of cSBl and anti-tumor action, and the results suggest that the replacement of the carboxylic group with an amide group is a useful strategy to increase the anti-tumor potency of cSBL.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the anti-tumour activity of cSAL is enhanced by the increase of net positive charge on the protein surface.
the anti-tumoral activity of cSAL increases with increasing net charge and that the replacement of the acidic amino acid residues with Arg is more effective than with Gln/Asn.
the replacement of the aspartic and glutamic acid residues of cSBP with arginine is effective in increasing its anti-tumor activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the net charge and the number of carboxyl groups modified with ethylenedimine contribute to the anti-tumor effect of cSBL.
the anti-tumoral effect of the sialic acid-binding lectin from bullfrogs is enhanced by the increase in net positive charge.
the anti-tumoral activity and internalization of cSBL into tumor cells are increased by increasing the net charge of the lectin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the replacement of aspartic acid or glutamic acid residues with arginine in cSBL enhances the anti-tumor effect of the lectin.
the replacement of acidic amino acid residues with basic amino acid residues is a promising approach for the development of anti-tumor agents.
we have identified the amino acid residues responsible for anti-tumor activity.
